title: Stack and Queue
summary: Brackets, monotonic stack, reverse Polish notation, histogram

guide.title: Order of work, made simple
points: A stack serves the most recent item first (last in, first out). A queue serves the oldest first (first in, first out).
Choosing the right one makes problems like bracket matching, undo and level-by-level search almost trivial.

guide.title: Stacks and queues around you
points: Undo / redo in editors and the browser back button are stacks.
Every function call goes on the call stack; that is how recursion works.
Code editors and compilers match brackets with a stack.
Print jobs, ticket booking queues and message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ) are queues; breadth-first search on maps and social graphs uses a queue.

guide.title: Push, pop, peek
points: Stack: push adds on top, pop removes the top, peek reads it. All O(1).
Queue: add at the back, remove from the front. A deque allows both ends.
Ask: does the newest item need attention first (stack), or the oldest (queue)?

guide.title: Stack and queue in your language
points: Use the fast structure: an array index or deque, not removing from the front of a list.

code.python:
stack = []
stack.append(1); stack.append(2)
stack.pop()                  # 2
from collections import deque
q = deque([1, 2])
q.popleft()                  # 1, O(1)

guide.title: Matching brackets
points: Push every opening bracket. A closing bracket must match the top; otherwise the text is invalid.
At the end the stack must be empty (nothing left open).

guide.title: Monotonic stack: the next greater element
points: Keep indices whose answer is not known yet; their values only decrease from bottom to top.
When a bigger value arrives, everything smaller on top has found its "next greater". Each index is pushed and popped once: O(n).
The same idea gives "days until warmer", stock span and the largest rectangle in a histogram.

guide.title: What breaks stack and queue code
points: Popping or peeking an empty stack: an exception in Java and Python, undefined behaviour in C++.
Using shift() (JavaScript) or list.pop(0) (Python) on a long queue: O(n) each time.
Java: prefer ArrayDeque over the old Stack class.
Forgetting the final check: brackets are valid only if nothing is left on the stack.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Signal words: "next greater / smaller", "previous", "span" → monotonic stack; "level by level", "minimum steps" → queue (BFS).
A deque of indices gives the maximum of every sliding window in O(n).
Classic designs: a min-stack with O(1) getMin, and a queue built from two stacks.
Next step: Recursion, which uses the call stack for you.

problems.title: Valid brackets
problems.statement: The string has only ()[]{} characters. Return true if every bracket is closed in the right order.
problems.hint: Push openings; each closing must match the top.

problems.title: Remove adjacent duplicates
problems.statement: Repeatedly remove two equal neighbouring letters until none are left. Return the result, or EMPTY.
problems.hint: Pop when the next letter equals the top.

problems.title: Evaluate reverse Polish notation
problems.statement: Evaluate the expression. Operators are + - * / ; division truncates toward zero.
problems.hint: Push numbers; an operator takes the two on top.

problems.title: Next greater element
problems.statement: For each element return the first larger element to its right, or -1.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Keep a stack of positions still waiting for a larger value.

problems.title: Days until warmer
problems.statement: For each day return how many days you wait for a warmer temperature, 0 if never.
inputFormat: temps: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: A stack of indices with falling temperatures.

problems.title: Sliding window maximum
problems.statement: Return the maximum of every window of k consecutive elements.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: A deque of indices whose values only decrease.

problems.title: Largest rectangle in histogram
problems.statement: Bars of width 1 have the given heights. Return the area of the largest rectangle that fits inside them.
inputFormat: heights: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: Increasing stack; when a lower bar arrives, close the taller ones.
